data.narrative:
Extropic, a Series A semiconductor company founded by Guillaume Verdon and Trevor McCourt, has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a semiconductor sector universe of 11 total peers: 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the $50M total raised as a proxy for current post-money value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median comparison was not feasible: while 12 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, similar valuation tier) returned insufficient datapoints for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring, though three semiconductor public companies trade at a median 21.4x price-to-sales, cannot be applied without Extropic's revenue—standard for unlisted companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $115M (high), with a median of $100M. This range reflects limited triangulation capacity rather than high conviction. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private financings at identical stage and burn profile, lack of disclosed revenue to benchmark against public multiples, and the early-stage nature of frontier semiconductor ventures, which exhibit wide performance dispersion. Refinement would require either revenue disclosure or access to recent comparable Series A or Series B transactions in chip design or manufacturing.
